text:
aisha: Heads up — staging multi-node TP run started hanging around 30s into generation. ~10% of requests hit timeouts. Repro on 4xA100 (p2p) with model v2.1-parted. Logs show rank(s) stuck waiting on all-reduce. :eyes:

Tom: can you paste the nccl / torch logs? and which commit?

 aisha: repro commit 0f3a9e7 (runtime: kernel selection tweak + new batching heuristic). stack excerpt:
 ```
 [2026-03-17 14:02:13] rank 2: waiting in ncclAllReduce at /opt/nccl/nccl.cpp:xxx
 [2026-03-17 14:02:13] rank 3: entering recv barrier
 [2026-03-17 14:02:13] rank 2: op=ALL_REDUCE size=256MB tag=0x7f
 ```
 also runtime trace shows long idle on ranks 2/3, while ranks 0/1 proceed.

 Priya: hmm could be imbalance from kernel selection + batching. Did the new heuristic push larger batches onto some partitions? That amplifies comm time. Any profiling from perf-bot?

 perf-bot: attaching perf trace (summarized) — synthetic run, same config:
 - compute time per microbatch (ms): [r0: 42, r1: 44, r2: 94, r3: 96]
 - all-reduce time (ms): [r0: 8, r1: 9, r2: 82, r3: 85]
 - overlap ratio (comm overlapped with compute): r0: 0.8, r2: 0.05
 Conclusion: severe imbalance on ranks 2/3, all-reduce not overlapping.

 Miguel: that smells like uneven token lengths/KV cache drift between ranks. If KV cache lengths diverge, some ranks will block waiting for tensors that never arrive. Any sign of different sequence lengths between partitions?

 aisha: interesting — we do have a KV cache reshuffle when we apply the new batching heuristic (to group similar lengths). I pushed a run with verbose KV logs. snippet:
 ```
 KV_CACHE: rank0 seq_len=128 entries=9
 KV_CACHE: rank1 seq_len=128 entries=9
 KV_CACHE: rank2 seq_len=127 entries=9
 KV_CACHE: rank3 seq_len=128 entries=9
 ```
 rank2 had seq_len=127 for some microbatches. That 1-token mismatch makes the TP pipeline step sizes shift.

 Tom: that 1-token mismatch could desync pipeline schedule — nice catch. Why would our batching heuristic allow a microbatch with seq_len off by one? edge-case in pad normalization?

 Priya: I dug through the heuristic: we normalize token lengths by rounding to the nearest multiple of 8 for kernel alignment; but we also have a post-filter that trims trailing padding for memory. If a microbatch crosses the boundary of a group, our trim can leave one rank with an extra real token (off-by-one).

 Miguel: repro script I used: run 4 ranks, partition sizes [0..1|2..3] and feed mixed lengths [127,128] with current heuristic. Minimal reproducer:
 ```python
 # pseudo
 for batch in batches:
   groups = heuristic.group_by_aligned_len(batch)
   kv_cache.update(groups)
   model.forward_kv(groups)
 ```
 Observed: schedules for pp stage 2 expect N tokens but recv gets N-1 -> nccl waits.

 aisha: quick mitigation: disable the trimming step in batching for multi-node TP (flip flag runtime.opt.strict_kv_lengths=true). That made the hang go away in staging. Will ship as hotfix config. :thumbsup:

 Tom: good. Longer term fixes?

 Priya: proposed fixes:
 - fix heuristic to preserve per-rank padded length invariants (always align and pad to same length across TP partitions)
 - add assertion in runtime: if kv_cache.len differs across ranks by >0 -> fail fast and dump trace instead of hang
 - add unit test in batching that simulates TP partitioning with edge-case lengths

 Miguel: also add a perf test: ensure all-reduce can overlap by forcing comm/compute reorder and assert overlap ratio > 0.4 for our baseline.

 infra-bot: deploy plan created: rollout config flip to staging at 14:45, monitor 30m, rollback on >1% timeouts. Ticket INF-3127.

 aisha: i'll post the kv-drift trace and link to the PR with the heuristic fix. PR will include the assert and a canary test.

 Priya: one more note — kernel selection tweak (preferring int8 path) increased compute variance across partitions because one partition got fallback to fp16 kernels due to shape mismatch. we should ensure kernel selection decisions are deterministic across TP ranks (same rules, same round-off). Otherwise that can amplify imbalance.

 Tom: right — add a gate: kernel-selection must be driven by model metadata + global config, not local heuristics. Add to board for next sprint.

 miguel: postmortem items drafted: 1) root cause: batching heuristic trim + nondeterministic kernel selection -> rank compute imbalance -> all-reduce blocking -> hang. 2) immediate mitigation: strict_kv_lengths flag. 3) mid-term: invariant checks + deterministic kernel policy. 4) perf: new overlap tests.

 aisha: thanks all. i'll follow up with PR link and a short playbook snippet for oncall (how to flip strict_kv_lengths and grab nccl traces). :white_check_mark:
